words.note: Casual; use 저 in polite speech. 나 + 가 → 내가.

ex.en: I'm hungry too.
I'll have coffee.
Want to watch a movie with me this weekend?

words.note: Pattern -지 않다; in speech 안 + verb is more common.

ex.en: It's not very cold today.
This food isn't spicy.
Minho doesn't drink alcohol.

words.note: Also "he" in writing; in speech say 그 사람.

ex.en: That movie was really fun.
Where is that store?
What's that person's name?

words.note: Sino-Korean numbers: 일 년, 이 년. 작년 = last year.

ex.en: It's been two years since I came to Korea.
I worked at this company for five years.
I travel once a year.

words.note: Also "my" for family/home: 우리 엄마, 우리 집.

ex.en: Let's have lunch together tomorrow.
My house is near the school.
Our team won!

words.note: Verb + -(으)ㄹ 때 = when ~.

ex.en: I lived in Busan when I was little.

ex.s: 밥 먹을 때 휴대폰 보지 마세요.
ex.r: bam meogeul ttae hyudaepon boji maseyo
ex.p: 밤 머글 때 휴대폰 보지 마세요
ex.en: Don't look at your phone while you eat.
When I'm tired, I go to bed early.

words.note: N + 중이다 = in the middle of N: 회의 중.

ex.en: I'm in a meeting right now.

ex.s: 이 두 개 중에서 뭐가 더 좋아요?
ex.r: i du gae jungeseo mwoga deo joayo
ex.p: 이 두 개 중에서 뭐가 더 조아요
ex.en: Which of these two is better?
I'm driving now, so I'll call you later.

words.note: 전화를 받다 = to answer the phone.

ex.en: Did you get a birthday present?
Do you take cards here?
Why didn't you answer the phone?

words.note: Only for close friends or younger people. 너 + 가 → 네가 (said 니가).

ex.en: Do you want to come too?
What are you doing today?
You're a really good cook!

words.note: ㄹ-irregular: 만들어요, 만드세요, 만든.

ex.en: I made gimbap.
My dad made this chair.
Making friends isn't easy.

words.note: 말하다 = to speak. Homonym: 말 = horse.

ex.en: Please speak slowly.
Is what you said true?
You speak Korean well.

words.en: to be visible; to look, seem
words.note: -아/어 보이다 = to look ~: 피곤해 보여요.

ex.en: You can see the ocean from here.
The letters are small, so I can't see well.
You look tired today.

words.note: N + 때문에; verb + -기 때문에.

ex.en: Traffic is bad because of the rain.
I couldn't go to school because of a cold.
I didn't buy it because it was too expensive.

words.note: 여자 친구 = girlfriend. Polite: 여자분.

ex.en: That woman is the teacher.
Where's the women's restroom?
Do you have a girlfriend, Minho?

words.en: to be unable to; to be bad at
words.note: One word for lack of ability or skill; circumstantial 'couldn't' is spaced: 못 했어요.

ex.en: I can't swim.
I can't drive yet.
I'm not good at cooking.

words.note: Short form 갖다. 가지고 가다 = to take along.

ex.en: Do you have a pen?
Can I have this?
Take an umbrella with you.

words.note: Joins sentences; between nouns use 하고 or 와/과.

ex.en: I ate. And then I took a walk.
Coffee, please. And some water too.
Did you do your homework? And clean your room?
Call me when you come out of the subway station.
When will the food come out?
This song was in a drama.

words.note: Same as 같이, slightly more formal.

ex.en: I had dinner with my family.
Let's take a picture together!
I went on a trip with a friend.

words.note: 남자 친구 = boyfriend. Polite: 남자분.

ex.en: Who is that man?
The men's restroom is on the second floor.
Ji-woo's boyfriend is a chef.

words.note: A sports match is 경기.

ex.en: I played video games at home on the weekend.
What games do you like?
My kid plays video games too much.
I really like this kind of weather.
Do you have this style in other colors?
Nothing like this has happened to me before.

words.note: N 위에 = on/above N. Opposite: 아래, 밑.

ex.en: The keys are on the desk.
Who lives upstairs?
Please put it on top of the fridge.

words.note: A bit formal; in speech -고 싶다 is more common.

ex.en: Choose the color you want.
If you want, let's go together.
I bought the present my child wanted.
Everyone laughed.
Everything on the menu is delicious.
Every room has air conditioning.

words.en: to look for, find; to withdraw (money)

ex.en: Did you find my phone?
I'm looking for the restroom.
I'll withdraw some money at the bank.
If there's a problem, get in touch.
Something's wrong with my car.
The test questions were too hard.
Let's talk somewhere quiet.
This is my favorite place.
There's no place to park.

words.note: N 안에. Different from the adverb 안 "not".

ex.en: What's in the bag?
I'll wait inside the building.
I'll arrive within an hour.

words.note: In casual speech 근데 is more common.

ex.en: It's expensive. But it's really good.
I want to go. But I don't have time.
I'm tired, but I'm happy.
What time does the movie start?
I'm starting yoga next week.
Let's start the meeting.

words.note: Same as 제일; 가장 is slightly more formal.

ex.en: Where's the nearest pharmacy?

ex.s: 여기서 가장 인기 있는 메뉴가 뭐예요?
ex.r: yeogiseo gajang ingi inneun menyuga mwoyeyo
ex.p: 여기서 가장 인기 인는 메뉴가 뭐예요
ex.en: What's the most popular dish here?
Family is the most important thing.
I'm going to sleep as soon as I get home.
The pharmacy is right next to the bank.
That's exactly what I mean.
Don't say things like that.
That's happened to me too.
Do you like that kind of movie?

words.note: N 앞에 = in front of N. Opposite: 뒤.

ex.en: Let's meet in front of the school.
Go straight ahead.
I sat in the front seat of the bus.

words.note: -아/어 죽겠다 = "so ~ I could die": 배고파 죽겠어요.

ex.en: I'm starving.
My pet fish died.
The flowers died because I didn't water them.

words.note: As "yeah" only with close friends; polite is 네.

ex.en: Oh, it's raining!
Oh, is it already ten?

ex.s: 어, 민호 씨! 여기서 뭐 해요?
ex.r: eo minho ssi yeogiseo mwo haeyo
ex.en: Oh, Minho! What are you doing here?

words.note: In casual speech 쓰다 is more common.

ex.en: Can I use this computer?
You can only use cash.
This app is easy to use.
It takes about 30 minutes.
I have about 10,000 won.
I study about two hours a day.

words.note: ㄷ-irregular: 들어요, 들었어요, 듣는.

ex.en: I like listening to music.
Did you hear about that?
I didn't catch that. Please say it again.
What did you do during vacation?
I waited for three hours.

ex.s: 제가 없는 동안 강아지 좀 봐 주세요.
ex.r: jega eomneun dongan gangaji jom bwa juseyo
ex.p: 제가 엄는 동안 강아지 좀 봐 주세요
ex.en: Please watch my dog while I'm away.

words.note: 마음에 들다 = to like (something).

ex.en: I like these clothes.
I've been feeling at ease lately.
Let me know if you change your mind.

words.note: Only before nouns: 첫날, 첫 번째.

ex.en: Today is my first day at the company.
How was your first date?
I bought my parents a gift with my first paycheck.
I have to go now.
It doesn't hurt anymore.
I can eat Korean food well now.

words.note: 사랑하다 = to love.

ex.en: I love you, Mom.
Do you remember your first love?
Our puppy gets a lot of love.

words.note: After -아/어 it means "completely": 잊어버리다.

ex.en: Please take out the trash.
I'll have to throw this milk out.
I threw out all my old clothes.

words.en: what kind of; which; a certain

ex.en: What kind of food do you like?
Which one is better?
Someone came looking for you.
The kids go to school at 8.
What are you doing after school?
I'm a teacher at this school.
I don't have much money.
I spent a lot of money this month.
Can you lend me some money?

words.note: ㄹ-irregular: 들어요, 드는. 마음에 들다 = to like.

ex.en: I'll carry your bag for you.
Don't lift heavy things.
Getting ready for a wedding costs a lot of money.
Why were you late?
I'm in a good mood for no reason.
Is there a reason you're learning Korean?

words.note: Also a noun: 모두가 = everyone.

ex.en: How much is it altogether?
Everyone in my family is healthy.
Is everyone here?
Wash your hands before eating.
My hands are so cold.
Raise your hand if you have a question.
There's a lot of food left over.
How much time is left?
I bought coffee with the leftover money.
Which team do you root for?
There are five people on our team.
The team dinner is on Friday.

words.note: 속이 안 좋다 = to have an upset stomach.

ex.en: My stomach is upset.
The key is in my pocket.
I saw my grandma in my dream.

words.note: Spoken short forms: 놔요, 놨어요.

ex.en: I'll put the keys here.
Put your bag on the chair.
I don't know where I put my phone.

words.note: Homonym: 밤 = chestnut.

ex.en: I couldn't sleep last night.
Don't walk around alone at night.
Sorry for calling so late at night.
I finished all my homework.
Did you eat it all?
Everyone in my family is tall.

words.note: 날씨 = weather; 생일날 = birthday.

ex.en: It's a nice day today.
What did you do on your birthday?
I'm leaving the next morning.

words.note: 줄(을) 서다 = to stand in line.

ex.en: Do I need to line up here?
The line is too long.
My earphone cord got tangled.

words.note: 약속을 잡다 = to make plans.

ex.en: I'll catch a taxi.
Hold on tight to the handle.
Let's make plans for next week.

words.note: 최고예요! = It's the best!

ex.en: This place's tteokbokki is the best.
Today's weather is perfect.
My mom is the best.

words.en: to pay; to hand in; to make (time)
words.note: 제가 낼게요 = It's on me.

ex.en: It's on me today.
When do I have to hand in the homework?

ex.s: 시간 좀 내 줄 수 있어요?
ex.r: sigan jom nae jul ssu isseoyo
ex.p: 시간 좀 내 줄 쑤 이써요
ex.en: Can you spare some time for me?
Do you have a good way to do it?
Do you know how to use this?
There's no other way.
What's that sound?
Please turn the volume down.

ex.s: 옆집 개 짖는 소리 때문에 못 잤어요.
ex.r: yeopjjip kkae jinneun sori ttaemune mot jjasseoyo
ex.p: 엽찝 깨 진는 소리 때무네 몯 짜써요
ex.en: I couldn't sleep because the neighbor's dog was barking.

words.note: Short for 아이. 애들 = kids.

ex.en: The kids are already asleep.
How old is your kid?
That kid is in my class.

words.note: N 뒤에 = behind N; -(으)ㄴ 뒤에 = after ~ing.

ex.en: There's a park behind my house.
Can I sit in the back?
Take the medicine after you eat.
This is an important document.
Health is the most important thing.
I have an important exam tomorrow.

words.note: Short for 그런데; very common in speech.

ex.en: By the way, what time is it?
It's tasty. But it's a bit salty.
But why didn't you call?

words.note: 잘 들어가세요 = "Get home safely."

ex.en: Please go inside.
Did you get home okay?
Can I go into the meeting room?

words.note: What is needed takes 이/가: 돈이 필요해요.

ex.en: Do you need help?
Do you need a bag?
You need a passport when you travel.

words.note: Spoken short form 얘기. 이야기하다 = to talk.

ex.en: Let's talk later.
Tell me an interesting story.
Grandma told us an old story.

words.note: 르-irregular: 불러요, 불렀어요.

ex.en: Come in when your name is called.
Should I call you a taxi?
I like singing.
What country are you from?
I like food from other countries too.
Is there a country you'd like to visit?
I've been feeling a lot of stress lately.
Did you feel the earthquake yesterday?
I felt a lot of things while traveling.

words.note: Often used as "actually": 사실은…

ex.en: Actually, today is my birthday.
Is that true?
Actually, I haven't done my homework yet.

words.note: ㅂ-irregular: 새로운, 새로워요. Before nouns, 새 is also common.

ex.en: I made a new friend.
There's a new item on the menu.
Everything about this job is new to me.

words.note: ㄹ-irregular: 힘들어요, 힘든.

ex.en: Work was really hard today.
It's hard to climb the stairs.
If you're tired, take a break.
Which city do you live in?
Seoul is a big city.
This city is really pretty at night.

words.note: 끝나다 = to end; 끝내다 = to finish.

ex.en: There's a café at the end of this street.
The end of the movie was a little sad.
Don't give up until the end.
Coffee without sugar, please.
I went out without an umbrella.
Can I go in without a reservation?
It's between the bank and the post office.
What's the relationship between you two?
We're close friends.

words.note: Homonym: 경기 = economy. A video game is 게임.

ex.en: Did you watch the soccer game yesterday?
What time does the match start?
My son is playing in a basketball game today.
Is this the last bus?
Let me ask just one last thing.
Today is the last day of class.
I read before bed.
Did you read my message?
Could you read me the menu?

words.note: 계획하다 = to plan. 계획을 세우다 = to make a plan.

ex.en: Do you have plans this weekend?
I made travel plans.
What are your plans for this year?

words.note: 두고 오다 = to leave something behind.

ex.en: I left my wallet at home.
Can I leave my bag here?
Where did you put the car keys?

words.note: 여러 가지 = various kinds.

ex.en: I've traveled to many countries.
I called several times.

ex.p: 이 빵지베는 여러 가지 빵이 이써요

words.note: Native numbers: 한 달, 두 달.

ex.p: 한 다레 한 번 머리를 잘라요
ex.en: I get a haircut once a month.
I'm moving next month.
The moon is really bright tonight.

words.note: 새해 = New Year. 올해 = this year.

ex.en: The sun is so hot.
It gets cold when the sun goes down.
Happy New Year!

words.note: Also 대학교. 대학생 = college student.

ex.en: Which college did you go to?
My daughter started college this year.
I met up with a friend from college.

words.note: In speech 벌써 is also very common.

ex.en: I already ate.
The tickets are already sold out.
I've already seen that movie.
A week has already gone by.
Does this bus go past City Hall?
This milk is past its expiration date.

words.note: 노래하다 = to sing. 노래방 = karaoke.

ex.en: What's the name of this song?
Do you want to go to karaoke?
My kid sings well.
Your room is really clean.
Do you have a room for tonight?
Did you clean your room?

words.note: 하루 종일 = all day.

ex.en: It rained all day.
How was your day?
How many glasses of water do you drink a day?

words.note: 가능하면 = if possible.

ex.en: Can I pay by card?
Is delivery possible tomorrow?
Please come early if you can.
Please give me some travel information.
There's a lot of information online.
Don't give out personal information over the phone.

words.note: 세상에! = "Oh my gosh!"

It's a small world!
This is the most delicious thing in the world.
This neighborhood is safe even at night.
Is it a safe place for kids to play?
The plane arrived safely.

words.note: Usually 알려 주다 (tell me) or humble 알려 드리다.

I'll let you know as soon as the results come out.
I told Mom the news first.
Check your text messages.
I double-checked the reservation time.
Could you check the bill, please?

words.note: 힘내세요! = Hang in there! / Cheer up!

ex.en: I'm so tired today that I have no energy.
You'll do great on the test. Hang in there!
Minho is really strong.

words.note: 출장 가다 = to go on a business trip.

ex.en: I'm going on a business trip to Busan next week.
My husband is on a business trip right now.
Have a good business trip!
Do you put sugar in your coffee?
Did you put an umbrella in your bag?

This restaurant raised its prices again.

A window seat, please.
There are four of us. Do you have a table?

ex.en: I had a strange dream last night.
My dream is to travel the world.
Sweet dreams!

words.note: 도움이 되다 = to be helpful.

ex.en: That was a big help. Thank you.
If you need help, tell me.

ex.p: 이 드라마 배우드리 연기를 정말 잘해요

ex.en: My father runs a small business.
How's business going?
I started a business with a friend.

ex.en: This problem is easier than I thought.
Hangul is easy to learn.
It's easy to get from the station to the hotel.

words.note: Someone else's son: 아드님 (honorific).

I have two sons.
I play soccer with my son on weekends.
What sports do you like?
When it comes to sports, I only like watching.
I watched the game at a sports bar with friends.

ex.en: My phone broke, so I went to the service center.
Try calling customer service.
I'm learning to swim at the local sports center.

words.en: to do so; to say so
words.note: Common forms: 그래요? (Really?), 왜 그래요? (What's wrong?)

ex.en: What's wrong? Did something happen?
Please don't do that.
Mom said it's going to rain tomorrow.
I'm really happy these days.
I'm happiest when I'm with my family.
Happy birthday! Have a happy day.

ex.en: Life is short.
This was the best trip of my life.

ex.p: 이 집 떡뽀끼는 제 인생 떡뽀끼예요

ex.p: 이 셔츠 다른 사이즈로 바꿀 쑤 이써요

I changed my phone password.

ex.r: jari jom bakkwo jusil ssu isseoyo
ex.p: 자리 좀 바꿔 주실 쑤 이써요
ex.en: Could you switch seats with me?
I like fruit, especially strawberries.
I'm especially tired today.
This restaurant's kimchi stew is especially good.

words.note: 해외여행 = a trip abroad.

ex.en: Have you ever traveled abroad?
My younger sibling works abroad.

ex.r: i kadeuneun haeoeeseodo sseul ssu isseoyo
ex.p: 이 카드는 해외에서도 쓸 쑤 이써요

words.note: Opposite: 유료 (paid). Never 'free' as in free time.

ex.en: Parking is free.
Water is free of charge.

ex.s: 이 앱은 한 달 동안 무료예요.
ex.r: i aebeun han dal dongan muryoyeyo
ex.p: 이 애븐 한 달 동안 무료예요
ex.en: This app is free for a month.

words.note: Used for struck instruments and racket sports: 피아노를 치다, 테니스를 치다.

ex.en: I play tennis every weekend.
My daughter plays the piano well.
My friend playfully hit my shoulder.

words.note: 아래층 = downstairs.

ex.en: The cat hid under the bed.
The restroom is one floor down.
The key is under the flower pot.

words.en: to be better; to get well
words.note: ㅅ-irregular: 나아요, 나았어요, 나으세요.

ex.en: This one is better than that one.
The subway is better than a taxi.
I hope your cold gets better soon.

words.note: Your own feelings; for others use 싫어하다.

ex.en: I hate rainy days.
I don't feel like going out today.
I don't like cucumber. Please leave it out.
I have a terrible headache.
Where does it hurt?

ex.p: 아이가 아파서 오늘 회사에 몯 까요

words.en: to take charge of; to keep (for someone)
words.note: Also 냄새를 맡다 = to smell something.

ex.en: I'll take care of this task.
Ji-woo is in charge of this project.

ex.s: 짐 좀 맡아 주실 수 있어요?
ex.r: jim jom mata jusil ssu isseoyo
ex.p: 짐 좀 마타 주실 쑤 이써요

Wow, that outfit looks great!
The view here is really amazing.
Thanks for the wonderful gift.
Come quick! The movie's starting.
We're late. Shall we walk a bit faster?
Time goes by really fast.

words.note: Counter with native numbers: 한 가지, 두 가지. 여러 가지 = various.

ex.p: 이 셔츠는 세 가지 새기 이써요

ex.en: I hope you get better soon.
I hope you get a good result.
I wish you both happiness.

words.note: Konglish: 서비스 also means a free extra from a shop.

ex.en: The service at this hotel is really good.
The internet service is down again.
The owner gave us dumplings on the house.
My grandmother lives in a small village.
This village is quiet and pretty.
We stayed two nights in a seaside village.
Who's your favorite soccer player?
Our son plays basketball for his school.
The players are coming onto the field.

words.note: 준비하다 = to prepare. 준비됐어요? = Are you ready?

ex.en: Are you all ready?
I'll take care of making dinner.
Are your trip preparations going well?

words.note: In speech usually 뭐; 무엇 sounds formal.

ex.en: How can I help you?
If you're curious about anything, just ask.
Above all, health is the most important thing.
I have a question!
If you have questions, ask anytime.
I got a lot of tough questions in the interview.

words.note: 화가 나다 = to get angry; 화내다 = to get mad at someone.

ex.en: Why are you so angry?
Please don't be mad. I made a mistake.
The traffic is so bad it's making me mad.

words.note: Humble form of 우리; not for Korea itself (say 우리나라).

ex.en: Come over to our place.
Our company starts at 9.
Our child is seven years old.
Until when is the sale?
It's exam period, so I'm really busy.
The weather was nice during the trip.

words.note: 감사합니다 is more formal than 고마워요.

ex.en: Thank you so much for your help.
Thank you for inviting me.
I sent my teacher a thank-you text.
I work out three times a week.
I was on Jeju Island for a week.
The package took a week to arrive.
How's life in Korea?
College life is really fun.
Work life is a bit hard.

words.note: Males say 형, females say 오빠. Also for close older male friends.

ex.en: I have one older brother.
Bro, want to grab something to eat?
My older brother works in the U.S.

words.note: Also 시계를 차다 = to wear a watch.

ex.en: The parking lot is already full.

The child kicked the ball hard.

words.note: 시작하다 = to start something.

ex.en: The movie is starting soon.
They say the rainy season starts next week.
Class starts at nine.

words.note: 사고가 나다 = an accident happens.

ex.en: There was a car accident on the street.
Traffic is really bad because of an accident.

words.note: Address and refer to them as 교수님.

ex.en: Professor, I have a question.
My older brother is a university professor.
The professor gave us a lot of homework.
I was so surprised at that moment.
Our wedding day was the happiest moment.
The moment I opened the door, the cat ran out.

words.note: -에 관심이 있다 = to be interested in.

ex.en: I'm very interested in cooking.
What are you into these days?
Thank you for your interest.
The train already left.
We're leaving on a trip early tomorrow morning.
It's been ten years since I left my hometown.

words.note: Someone else's daughter: 따님 (honorific).

ex.en: My daughter is learning to swim these days.
I have two daughters.
I went shopping with my daughter.

words.note: Konglish: means any website, not just its main page.

ex.en: Check the website for details.
I made a reservation on the restaurant's website.
What's the company's website address?
I couldn't sleep properly last night.
Did you understand this explanation properly?
Please eat proper meals.
This café has a nice vibe.

ex.en: I have a feeling something good will happen today.
What was your first impression of him?
How many dollars is this?
I exchanged dollars for won at the airport.
It's five dollars for a cup of coffee.

words.note: For children or someone younger; 젊다 = young (adult).

ex.en: My younger sibling is three years younger than me.
I lived in Busan when I was little.

words.note: 나눠요 in polite speech.

ex.en: Shall we split the pizza in half?
I had a chat with my coworkers.
We'll split into two teams.
I ordered it online.
Class is online today.
They sell it cheaper online.

The bride was so beautiful.
The lyrics of this song are beautiful.

Let's go together next time.
I hope I get a chance to go to Korea.

Anything is fine with me.
Call me anytime.

The weather is strange today.

You have to follow the school rules.

History class is the most fun.

The internet here is really fast.
Delivery was faster than I expected.
They're my favorite author.
That writer's new book is out.
Wei is a webtoon artist.

words.note: Passive 막히다: 길이 막혀요 = traffic is jammed.

ex.en: A car is blocking the road.
Water was leaking, so I blocked it with a towel.
Mom stopped us from going.

I have lots of good memories here.
Do you remember my name?

Let's talk in person.
I went to the store and bought it in person.
I go to church every Sunday.
I ate with friends from church.
There are many churches near our house.

words.en: to fall into; (weight, hair) come off
words.note: 살이 빠지다 = to lose weight; 사랑에 빠지다 = to fall in love.

The two of them fell in love.
You've lost a lot of weight!
I watch the news every morning.
The news says it'll rain tomorrow.
I read the news on my phone.

words.note: Two words with the same spelling: street and distance.

ex.en: There are a lot of people on the street.
There are lots of cafes on this street.
It's within walking distance.

words.note: 남동생 = younger brother; 여동생 = younger sister.

ex.en: I have two younger siblings.
I live with my younger sibling.
My younger sibling is a college student.

words.en: to end up; what to do (어쩌죠?)
words.note: Short for 어찌하다. 어쩌다가 as an adverb also means "by chance."

ex.en: How did you get hurt?
What do we do now?
Somehow I ended up being late.

words.note: 그림을 그리다 = to draw a picture.

ex.en: Who drew this picture?
I take drawing lessons every weekend.
The child drew a picture of Mom.

words.note: 축구하다 = to play soccer.

ex.en: I play soccer with friends on weekends.
Did you watch the soccer game yesterday?
My son is learning soccer at school.

words.note: Everyday "run" is often 뛰다. Homonym 달리다 = to hang, be attached.

words.note: Goes before a noun (새 차). The adjective is 새롭다.

words.note: A filler while thinking.

My job is to prepare the meetings.
Dad plays a big role at home.
The wind is strong today.
This coffee is a bit strong.
My mom is a really strong person.

words.note: 잊어버리다 is very common in speech. 잊지 마세요 = don't forget.

ex.en: Don't forget your umbrella.
I forgot my password.
I'll never forget that day.
The whole store is on sale.
The whole team went to the work dinner.
Please show me the full menu.
Let's meet at 3 p.m.
They say it'll rain in the afternoon.
Are you free this afternoon?
Forget the past.
I wish I could go back in time.
The Korean past tense is hard.

words.note: 부탁해요 / 부탁드려요 (more polite) = please.

I understand how you feel.

words.note: Spoken form of 이야기하다.

words.note: Used for online reviews; 리뷰 is also common.

This cafe is spacious.
